newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI says sells mine stake to Metorex.
newsitem.headline: JCI says sells mine stake to Metorex.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd said on Tuesday it had sold its 33 pct stake in Consolidated Murchison to Metorex Pty Ltd for an undisclosed sum.

JCI said in a statement it had supported Consolidated Murchison, the world's largest producer of antimony, with 10.4 million rand's worth of loan finance but it was viewed as a poor fit, primarily due to its size.

"The mine is a marginal operation at current commodity prices and as such its future viability, though not guaranteed, will be greatly enhanced by a management team with the experience and skills necessary to enhance the profitability of small marginal operations," it said.

Consolidated Murchison mines in the Letaba district of South Africa for antimony ore, from which it produced 9,413 tonnes of antimony concentrates in the year to June 30, 1996. Gold and silver are recovered as by-products.
